sentences.text: The genus name Wannanosaurus means "Wannan lizard" and refers to the location where fossils were found. The species Wannanosaurus yansiensis was described by Hou Lian-Hai in 1977.
The animal is known from a single partial skeleton consisting of a partial skull roof, lower jaw, femur, tibia, rib fragments, and other pieces.
Its flat skull roof with large openings suggests it was a primitive member of the pachycephalosaur group.
Fossils of Wannanosaurus were found in red sandstone sediments of the Xiaoyan Formation in Anhui, China.
Wannanosaurus was likely a herbivore or omnivore that fed close to the ground on plants and possibly insects.
Wannanosaurus was sometimes classified in the now-deprecated family Homalocephalidae, which grouped pachycephalosaurs lacking domed skulls.
A cladogram based on analyses by Butler and colleagues from 2011 shows the classification of Wannanosaurus.

Wannanosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous in the Maastrichtian, approximately 72 to 69 million years ago in what is now Asia, while the broader time range for the Maastrichtian spans from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
